role: one switchable hero-tree candidate in the Chapter 2 round-3 comparison lab
technique: leader repair: round-1's nine accepted poses restyled in batched reference-mode edits onto one shared 32-colour palette, then densified with pinned interpolations

referencePlate.usedAs: two-panel style plate built deterministically from the real Studio island render: left = the island body untouched, right = the same facets hue-rotated to foliage green and bark brown
referencePlate.neverComposited: the experiment DID composite previews on the real island plate (preview-on-island.gif, on-island-strip.png); those are review aids, not assets

anchorRegistration.appliedRule: alpha-weighted x across bottom three occupied rows; bottom-most occupied y
anchorRegistration.appliedRuleSource: round-1's accepted track (assets/chapter2-organic-pose-to-pose/tree-registration.json), re-derived here and verified to reproduce that track's (96,188) on all nine accepted frames
anchorRegistration.experimentDeclaredRule: alpha-weighted x over the 10-row band 32..22 px above the bottom-most opaque row (the trunk axis above the root flare); groundY = bottom-most opaque row
anchorRegistration.registeredAnchorClaim: every frame's alpha-weighted contact x lies within maxAnchorResidualPx of the registered integer anchor, and its bottom-most occupied row IS the registered y exactly. Stated as a BOUND rather than an equality because a frame can land exactly on the 0.5 tie, where round-to-nearest is not a total function and Python (half-to-even) and JavaScript (half-up) disagree; at a tie the registration prefers not to move the art.

costOfApplyingTheAppliedRule.note: Re-pinning to the ground contact under round-1's rule moves the tree body by this much. Where 'after' is worse than 'before', the experiment's own band was averaging a wider part of the base and was more stable for the BODY even though it was not measuring the CONTACT.

tracks.prompt: Restyle the colours only. Keep the exact same silhouette, the same pose, the same branch layout and every leaf and root exactly where it is. Take the palette, the soft cream-and-brown outline, the flat facet shading and the gentle low contrast from the reference plate: turn the near-black outline into a warm mid brown, mute the greens toward a soft sage olive, warm and desaturate the bark, and flatten the glossy highlights into flat blocks of colour. It must still read as a green leafy tree on a fully transparent background.

restyle.model: PixelLab edit_image (reference mode, 3 frames per call at 128 px)

tracks.sharedWith: every candidate in the lab, and with chapter2-organic-pose-to-pose-v1
tracks.note: FIXED across the lab (ADR-0277 D2 retained cutout/pose plant track). Registered here by reference, not copied, so a candidate swap cannot change the plant.

authoringRejects.reason: vendor POLICY refusal (seed 31600): imperative 'erase/delete' wording trips the filter; the same instruction phrased positively passed
path not taken (seed 31605): all nine restyled in one 64 px call - consistent but soft and dusty
grew a tan soil mound and a detached canopy blob
overshoot; the pair also did not need densifying (+3.7%)
zero frames landed between the endpoints; f04->f05 is a lateral morph, not growth
seedling kept the adult root flare under a stub stem; reads as a cut stump

knownWeakness: a repair, not a re-authoring. Frames 15-18 are near-static variants of round-1's mature poses (+5.0%, +0.2%, +1.6%) that wobble rather than settle, and the frame 14->15 handoff still changes the trunk to its buttressed multi-stem form in one step.

appOwns: world sockets, depth slots and painter order
app-native SVG coast and ground reveal
the even progress mapping across the delivered frame order

budget.ceilingPolicy: the restated ceiling IS the measured actual - zero headroom by design, so adding a byte, a frame or a layer fails validation rather than sliding through
budget.mountedAtOnce: ONE hero-tree track over the one shared plant track. The other three candidates are checked in but are never decoded in the same session.
